classification.difficultyReason: Uses a shared right triangle to express two angles and deduce an inverse trigonometric identity.

spec.description: Unshaded right triangle with a horizontal base, vertical right side, angle arcs at the two acute vertices and a right-angle square at the lower-right vertex. Ordinary source marks are rendered in house black.
spec.mathematics: Hypotenuse 1; vertical side x; lower-left angle A; upper-right angle B. The nondegenerate triangle implies 0<x<1.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and labels are permanent question givens.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find an expression for $A$ in terms of $x$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find a similar expression for $B$ in terms of $x$.

answer.worked:
The two acute angles in a right-angled triangle sum to $\frac{\pi}{2}$.

$$\begin{aligned}A+B&=\frac{\pi}{2}\\\sin^{-1}x+\cos^{-1}x&=\frac{\pi}{2}\end{aligned}$$
